name: pipeline
summary: Sequential processing chain: a payload accumulates data and errors as ordered processors run.
description: Creates the pipeline pattern: a payload, a processor interface, and a pipeline runner
problem: Data must flow through multiple processing steps in a defined order — each step examining, transforming, or accumulating information — without the steps knowing about each other. Errors need tracking across the whole run, and any step must be able to halt the chain.
appliesWhen: An operation decomposes into ordered, independent steps (validate, enrich, calculate, finalize)
Steps accumulate or transform shared state as the data flows through
Errors at any step must be collected and visible at the end of the run
Steps should stay decoupled — communicating only through the shared payload
avoidWhen: The workflow is two or three fixed calls — a service method is simpler and clearer
Consumers react to a fact without ordering guarantees — use an event with listeners
Steps need request/response interaction with each other — pipelines share only the payload
The steps run asynchronously or across requests — use tasks and handlers instead
examples: Build an order calculation pipeline: inventory, discounts, tax, shipping, total
I need a report generation flow with independent accumulating steps
Process an import through validation, normalization, and persistence stages
Chain processors that can each veto the operation
tradeoffs: Three files and an extra indirection per step. Worth it when steps genuinely vary or reorder; overkill for short fixed sequences. Processor order matters and inter-step data dependencies are implicit — document what each processor expects and provides on the payload.
outputs: A {name}Payload class that accumulates data, tracks errors, and supports halting
A {name}Pipeline runner that executes processors in order and honors stop()
postApply: Create a processor class per step implementing {name}Processor, each focused and independent
Replace the payload's generic data bag with typed properties and purpose-named accessors
Order processors deliberately when constructing the pipeline — dependencies flow forward
Add a final processor that verifies required data, handles accumulated errors, and produces the result
Compose the pipeline where it is consumed (or bind it via a DI factory) with the processors in order

name.description: Domain name for the pipeline (e.g. ReportGeneration)
name.aiHint: PascalCase phrase naming the overall operation, no suffix — the recipe derives {name}Pipeline, {name}Payload, {name}Processor (ReportGeneration, OrderCalculation).
